notes: The San Francisco City Planning Commission's minutes of its regular and special meetings, January to December 1973, from the volumes the San Francisco Public Library contributed to the Internet Archive (24minutesofsanfran1973sa, 25minutesofsanfran1973sa, 26minutesofsanfran1973sa, 27minutesofsanfran1973sa). Pages were split from the hOCR search text on the Internet Archive page index, counting the viewer page among the leaves scandata.xml does not mark addToAccessFormats=false (checked against the scan of 24minutesofsanfran1973sa n10, page 4 of the 4 January 1973 minutes). Every page is dated from the meeting header it sits under. Four kinds of finding: what the Commission decided about a property, dated to the meeting that decided it; what the minutes state stood on or occupied the property; dated past facts the minutes state about a building; and landmark designations. A proposal on its own is not a finding. A Board of Supervisors action the minutes report without its own date is framed 'by' the date of the meeting that reported it. The minutes name applicants, owners, attorneys, objectors, commissioners and staff throughout; the reader spec (in research/sources/sf-planning-commission-minutes.md, under Reader spec) barred all of them from every field, and kept companies, institutions, named buildings and architects.

coverage.remaining: Every page of the four 1973 volumes (24minutesofsanfran1973sa, 25minutesofsanfran1973sa, 26minutesofsanfran1973sa, 27minutesofsanfran1973sa) was read. Volumes 28-29 (1974) are read in minutes-1974.json; volumes 30-39 (1975-1980) and 40-58 (1994-2005) remain. Of the 287 unresolved, 180 print no street number: they are located only by a corner, a bearing, a block, or a building name with no page to carry it (the Pacific Medical Center and UC Medical Center blocks, the Southern Pacific depot at Fourth and Townsend, the Greenwich Square and Kite Hill rezonings, Mira Glen, the Twin Peaks reservoir, St. Mary's Hospital's master plan, the city's surplus-lot sales); 39 have no EAS record at the number (2065 Sacramento, 1330 Clay, 1850 Newcomb, 1446 5th Avenue); 3 are condominium parcels waiting on #228 and #446 (1452-54 Waller, 1170 Sacramento); the rest are ranges now split across parcels, lots of several parcels, or OCR-mangled numbers whose building another finding already placed.
coverage.note: 872 OCR pages with text out of 1,750 scanned leaves, read by seven parallel readers from one written spec (the dossier's Reader spec section); 49 meetings dated from their own headers; 457 findings: 217 statements of what stood on a property, 181 decisions, 43 dated past facts, 16 landmark designations. Every quote was re-anchored mechanically against its own page (457 of 457; one moved to the facing page). 170 resolved: 145 by the EAS join on a printed number, 25 by hand — 8 by the record's own block and lot, 17 by name on a building the site already carries, including the Lilienthal-Orville Pratt House, which EAS files at 1820 California on two parcels and the join put on the wrong one, and the Haslett Warehouse, whose header prints 600 Beach (the Cannery's parcel) and whose resolution prints 680. Four EAS joins were taken back to unresolved: a condominium unit pair at 1452-54 Waller, a point short of its number at 3226 25th Street, and the 71-owner condominium at 1170 Sacramento. 147 published on 88 pages (44 of them seeded, 2 Golden Gate Park place pages); 23 declined: 9 already on the page from another source or an earlier volume, 4 too thin to add to what the page says, 5 procedural (postponements, a withdrawn request), 2 OCR-misread years, 2 repeats within the batch, 1 block-wide statement.
